This page has no panzoom, and every Python (Jupyter) figure opens in lightbox.
Its cases are the same as on [panzoom on every figure](k-jupyter-auto.html), so
each one can be compared with the case of the same number there. The R cases are
on the [lightbox page](a-lightbox.html) and [panzoom on every
figure](c-panzoom-auto.html).

```yaml
lightbox: true
```

Jupyter leaves the `panzoom` and `lightbox` options out of the code shown on the
page. The **Code** button at the top shows the full source.

The plots share this setup:

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

x = np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, 400)
```

## Figure with a caption {#c1 expect-open="glightbox"}

A Python figure with a caption. It opens in lightbox.

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a sine wave"
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(x))
plt.show()
```

## Plot without a caption {#c2 expect-open="glightbox"}

A plot without a caption. It opens in lightbox.

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a cosine wave"

plt.plot(x, np.cos(x))
plt.show()
```

## Subfigures {#c3 expect-open="glightbox"}

One cell with two plots, made subfigures by `fig-subcap`. Either one opens in
lightbox, in a two-image gallery.

```{python}
#| label: fig-pair
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave and a cosine wave, sin(2x) and cos(2x)."
#| fig-subcap: ["Sine", "Cosine"]
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "Line plot of a sine wave"
#|   - "Line plot of a cosine wave"
#| layout-ncol: 2

plt.plot(x, np.sin(2 * x))
plt.show()
plt.plot(x, np.cos(2 * x))
plt.show()
```

## lightbox options {#c4 expect-open="glightbox"}

One cell with two plots and `lightbox:` options for a group and a description.
With Jupyter, lightbox ignores these options, so each plot opens in lightbox on
its own, without the group or description.

```{python}
#| lightbox:
#|   group: waves
#|   description: "Ignored by lightbox with Jupyter."
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "Line plot of a sine wave"
#|   - "Line plot of a cosine wave"

plt.plot(x, np.sin(3 * x))
plt.show()
plt.plot(x, np.cos(3 * x))
plt.show()
```

## lightbox off {#c5 expect-open="nothing"}

A cell with `lightbox: false`. Clicking the plot does nothing.

```{python}
#| lightbox: false
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a sine wave"
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave, sin(4x)."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(4 * x))
plt.show()
```

## panzoom on a cell {#c6 expect-open="glightbox"}

A cell with `#| panzoom: true`. The panzoom filter isn't loaded on this page, so
the option does nothing, and the plot opens in lightbox.

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a cosine wave"
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap: "A cosine wave, cos(4x)."

plt.plot(x, np.cos(4 * x))
plt.show()
```

## Markdown image {#c7 expect-open="glightbox"}

A markdown image alone in a paragraph. It opens in lightbox.

```markdown {.show-source}
![Sunset at Chilmark Beach, Martha's Vineyard.](../../images/mv-0.jpg){fig-alt="Sunset over a sandy beach, with a tall rock stack against the sun"}
```

## Opt out of lightbox {#c8 expect-open="nothing"}

A markdown image with `.nolightbox`, which keeps lightbox off it, so clicking it
does nothing.

```markdown {.show-source}
![Waves breaking below the clay cliffs at Aquinnah, Martha's Vineyard.](../../images/mv-1.jpg){.nolightbox fig-alt="Waves breaking below grassy clay cliffs at Aquinnah"}
```

## Caption on the left {#c9 expect-open="glightbox" expect-desc-position="bottom"}

A cell with `desc-position: left` under both the `panzoom` and the `lightbox`
cell options. panzoom is off, so it opens in lightbox, and with Jupyter,
lightbox ignores its nested options, so the caption shows below the image.

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a sine wave with a long period"
#| panzoom:
#|   desc-position: left
#| lightbox:
#|   desc-position: left
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave with a long period."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(x / 2))
plt.show()
```
